fixes: Line 4 ph (open_loop, PH audience): 'palihim na *dinodoble* ng utak mo' means 'secretly DOUBLES', which gives away the ~2x that the English line withholds until line 5. Use a neutral verb that matches 'multiplies', e.g. 'Kasi palihim na *pinalalaki* ng utak mo ang isang side ng coin.'

Line 1 (hook): the 'say' text is 15 words (~5.8 s), so the question 'Do you flip?' does not land until almost 6 s. Tighten the spoken line to e.g. 'Heads, you win one-fifty. Tails, you lose a hundred. Flip?' (~10 words) so the tension peaks inside 4 s. The on-screen '+$150 / -$100' already carries the dollar signs.

Lines 3-5 (open_loop): the brain half of the loop is named at line 5, which starts at ~16.5 s of ~43 s (~38%, not ~45% as the open_loop field says). After that, only the implicit 'math says yes' loop remains. Make it explicit in line 3 or 4 so it carries to the end, e.g. line 3: 'The math says yes, and by a lot. So why does your brain say no?' Then line 9 (<2%) pays off 'by a lot'.

Line 5 (escalation): at 15 spoken words (~5.8 s), this is the joint-longest beat and stacks three ideas: the name, '150 studies', and '2x'. The '150 studies' tag is already on screen, so drop it from the voice: 'Loss aversion: losses hurt about twice as much as wins.' (~4 s).

Line 6 / line 8 (clarity): the 'say' text drops 'dollars' ('about one ninety five', 'up twenty five hundred'), which is easy to mishear on first watch, and 'one ninety five' can sound like a time. Say 'about a hundred ninety-five dollars' and 'up twenty-five hundred dollars', or trim elsewhere to make room.

Line 9 / line 10 (payoff/surprise): '<2%' is the real 'wait, what?', but it is not tied back to the brain. Add a 3-5 word bridge before line 10, e.g. a spoken half-line in line 9 such as 'Under two percent. Your brain still says no.' This makes the payoff land on the viewer's own bias instead of on arithmetic. The Kahneman $150/$100 flip is familiar to psych-Shorts viewers, so the surprise has to come from this contrast.
Line 10 (ending): 'Tails, a hundred' loses the 'lose' and is ambiguous by ear. Say 'Tails, lose a hundred.' Also, keep the caveat 'One flip's still 50/50' as short as it is now. Do not let it grow.

Originality: Benny's hand-freeze in line 2 helps, but the spoken script is still a textbook Kahneman recap. Give Benny one voiced personal reaction at the twist (line 7 or 9), e.g. Benny muttering 'Wait... I've been saying no?' before line 10, so the story is Benny discovering his own bias.

notes.verdict_1am_viewer: Would stop: yes. It is an instant second-person money question with +$150 / -$100 burned in at frame 0. Would stay: likely to the end now. Line 4's tease and the tighter 2x -> $195 beat fixed v1's sag, and the 100-flip / <2% numbers give a real reason to wait. The remaining drag is the long spoken line 1 and line 5.
